naive_assumption: Our agent factory is running fast because LLMs generate code in seconds and unit tests pass in 30 seconds.
empirical_reality: Telemetry measured average task lead time at 10.4 hours (37,620s), while active execution was only 25 minutes. 95% of task lifecycle was spent idling in queue waiting for human manual triage.
mechanism: Autonomous cron-based intake and worker assignment that pairs open issues to persistent worker lanes continuously without human polling.
tweet_hook: We thought our AI coding factory was hyper-fast because tests passed in 30s. Then we measured lead time: tasks spent 95% of their life idling in queues waiting for human triage (10.4 hours avg). Here is how automated issue assignment unlocked true continuous flow 🧵👇
ru_summary: Иллюзия скорости AI-фабрики: LLM пишет код за минуты, тесты проходят за 30 секунд, но средний lead time задачи составлял 10.4 часа. 95% времени задача просто висела в очереди в ож��дании внимания человека. Автономный крон-диспетчер перевел фабрику из пакетной ручной обработки в непрерывный конвейер.

naive_assumption: Autonomous cron dispatchers can simply spawn subagents or workers whenever an issue is detected.
empirical_reality: Without atomic claiming, automated crons spawned duplicate workers on the same tasks, causing git state collisions and race conditions.
mechanism: Single-writer immutable ledger with atomic OS file locking (fcntl.flock + os.fsync) and explicit claim/intake states.
tweet_hook: Why naive multi-agent systems crash when you automate them: the moment you remove human dispatch, agents race to claim the same tasks. True autonomy requires single-writer ledgers and OS-level file locking (fcntl.flock). Here is why 🧵
ru_summary: Парадокс параллелизма: убирая человека из диспетчеризации, вы моментально получаете гонку агентов за одни и те же задачи и конфликты в git. Автономия невозможна без атомарной блокировки (fcntl.flock) и строго однопоточного журнала состояний (single-writer ledger).

topic: The Inspector's Trap: External Audit vs Self-Audit
naive_assumption: A governance agent should inspect member codebases from the outside with regex, file checks, and test counting.
empirical_reality: External inspection is shallow, causes token bloat, and encourages gaming. Quality is ignored by member HQs until audit day.
mechanism: The two-tier quality model: teach member factories to audit themselves via standardized tools/audit.py, and audit the integrity of their auditing process (cadence, ledger sequence, gate bite).
tweet_hook: Stop building AI 'inspector' agents that grade other codebases from the outside. It doesn't scale. Build self-auditing factories with internal telemetry (ISO 9001 for AI agents) and audit the audit instead 🧵
ru_summary: Ловушка инспектора: внешний агент-аудитор тратит тысячи токенов на поверхностный парсинг чужого кода, пока фабрики игнорируют качество. Решение: дать каждой фабрике встроенный инструмент самоаудита (tools/audit.py), а на верхнем уровне проверять математическую целостность их измерений.

topic: Substrate Feedback Loops & Autonomous Topic Binding
naive_assumption: Agent frameworks provide complete out-of-the-box infrastructure for autonomous factory operation.
empirical_reality: Autonomous lanes could not bind themselves to Telegram forum topics without a human sending the first message (kickstarting deadlock).
mechanism: Fleet supplier-client loop: member factories experience runtime friction, advise harness maintainers (OpenCrabs Issue #170), and unlock native topic auto-binding (action: bind_topic).
tweet_hook: The hidden hurdle of agent factories: autonomous workers that can't speak until a human talks first. How empirical fleet feedback between member factories and the OpenCrabs harness led to native topic auto-binding (#170) 🧵
ru_summary: Замкнутый круг запуска: автономный агент не мог привязаться к Telegram-топику, пока человек не напишет первое сообщение. Решение: петля обратной связи между фабриками и разработчиками харнесса OpenCrabs привела к внедрению нативной автопривязки топиков (Issue #170).
